method: Questions were researched with an evidence-only retrieval tool over one corpus of open-access and public-domain texts (see corpus.json). Each excerpt was checked word for word against the corpus passage it cites when this file was written; corpus_chunk numbers that passage in the corpus snapshot of 2026-10-01.
questions: How did falsafa and kalām differ in their approach to knowledge and causation?
What role did demonstration play in Arabic philosophy's theory of knowledge?
What is Ibn Sīnā's theory of ḥads, and why is his epistemology called a rationalist empiricism?
What was the floating man thought experiment meant to show, and how was it received?
What was al-Ghazālī's skeptical crisis, and how did it end?
What exactly did al-Ghazālī deny about causation, and on what grounds?
How did Ibn Rushd reply on causation and on philosophy and religion?
What is Suhrawardī's knowledge by presence?
How did these ideas reach Latin Europe?
